conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, this is Officer David Miller, badge ID 674219. Whom am I speaking with?
Oh, yes, hello, my name is Elaine Myers. I got a message saying there was a problem with my taxes?
Yes, Mrs. Myers. We have identified significant discrepancies in your federal tax returns from 2019 through 2022. The IRS has flagged your file for immediate review.
I... I don't understand. I thought I did everything right. I just get Social Security, sir.
According to Section 7201 of the Internal Revenue Code, there's an outstanding tax liability, including accrued interest and federal penalties. The amount currently stands at $7,980.15.
That's impossible! I don't owe that kind of money. I can't pay that!
Mrs. Myers, this is a federal matter. If this balance is not settled today, the IRS will initiate a lien on your bank accounts and notify Social Security for immediate withholding of your benefits.
No, no, please! I need those benefits to live. Can't you check again? Maybe it's a mistake?

If you wish to dispute the charges, you will need to appear before a magistrate in federal court. However, this will also result in your Medicare and Social Security accounts being temporarily frozen until the case is resolved.
I can't go to court. I don't have anyone to help me. Is there any other way?

We can arrange an immediate out-of-court settlement if you comply with IRS resolution protocols today. First, I need to confirm your identity for security. Can you verify your full home address and date of birth?
Uh, yes, I live at 147 Grover Lane, Springfield, Illinois, and my birthday is March 18, 1948.
Thank you, Mrs. Myers. For further verification, please state the last four digits of your Social Security number.

Alright, your information matches our records. Due to the severity of your case, you are required to make an immediate payment to halt enforcement actions such as asset seizure, wage garnishment, and arrest.
I don't have that kind of money! I only have my small savings.
You may settle the balance partially today to prevent escalation. The IRS now accepts secure electronic payments via wire transfer, cryptocurrency, or prepaid gift cards.
Crypto? I don't know anything about that. I do have a credit card, but the limit is low.
Understood. You can purchase prepaid Target or Amazon gift cards up to your available limit. Once you have them, read me the codes so we can process your settlement and stop further action.
Is that really how the IRS does this? Gift cards?

This is a secure emergency protocol authorized for high-risk cases like yours. Failure to comply within the next hour will result in immediate referral to the U.S. Marshals for arrest and your assets being frozen.
Oh, please, I don't want any trouble. How many cards do I need to buy?

As much as your available credit allows. Typically, cards are sold in $500 denominations. After purchasing, remain on the line and read each code aloud to me. Do not hang up or consult anyone, as this is a confidential federal investigation.
Okay, I... I'll go now. But please, promise me I won't lose my Social Security.
As long as you follow instructions exactly, your benefits will remain active and no charges will be filed. How much credit do you have available on your card?
Maybe $1,200, I'm not sure.
That will suffice for now. Purchase two $500 Target gift cards and one $200 card. Call me back immediately and provide the codes for processing. Do not delay or involve any third party.
